ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: When an airplane goes from diving to pulling up, the pilot is in an overweight state. At this time, the supporting force of the seat on the pilot is greater than the gravity acting on the pilot; this phenomenon is called overload. Excessive overload will cause the pilot's limbs to become heavy, the brain to suffer ischemia, temporary blindness, and even fainting. Specially trained air force pilots can withstand at most the influence of 9 times gravity. Take g as $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$; then when the speed of the airplane diving and pulling up along a circular-arc trajectory in a vertical plane is 100 m/s, the minimum radius of the circular-arc trajectory is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem text gives: the pilot can withstand at most the influence of 9 times gravity, speed v=100 m/s, g=10 m/s^2. The airplane going from diving to pulling up near the lowest point can be regarded as circular motion in a vertical plane, with the centripetal direction vertically upward. Analyze the forces on the pilot: the seat supporting force N is upward, gravity mg is downward, and the resultant force provides the centripetal force, so N - mg = mv^2/r. Withstanding at most 9 times gravity means the maximum supporting force N=9mg. To find the minimum radius of the circular-arc trajectory, take the critical case: 9mg - mg = mv^2/r, that is, 8mg = mv^2/r; cancel m to get 8g = v^2/r. Therefore r = v^2/(8g) = 100^2/(8×10) = 10000/80 = 125 m.
